evaluations.label: A
errors: "Target group 15-35 years" is presented as a settled decision; the transcript shows the group never settled an age range (15-35, under 65, teenagers and families, 20-55 were all floated) and the Project Manager concluded it was more useful to define objectives like fashion and simplicity than an age target.

Action item "Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery" was not assigned in the meeting; the User Interface Designer only said they should maybe investigate whether it needs a battery at all, and the cradle idea was simply kept.
Action item "Provide updated market research data" is listed as unassigned, but the Marketing Expert explicitly said she would e-mail more age numbers before the next meeting.
The real closing actions (questionnaire and summary for each member, Project Manager posting minutes and slides, the three individual concept assignments) are missing from the action items.
strengths: Market research numbers (75%, 80%, 10% of buttons, over 50% losing remotes) are correct.

Correctly records teletext exclusion, TV-only scope, 12.5 euro production limit, voice recognition rejected on price, and the agreed functions (large essential buttons, hidden extras, loss prevention).
Timestamps make it easy to jump to the recording.
weaknesses: Very telegraphic; fragments like "80% willing pay more for style" and "Avoid overload with audio settings" give little context to someone who missed the meeting.
Omits the 25 euro retail price, the corporate slogan, the sliding-panel idea, RSI, the LCD screen mention, and the shared-folder problem.
Misstates the target group as decided and misses the actual assigned work, so a reader would not know who does what next.

evaluations.label: B
errors: "Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder" is wrong: the Industrial Designer confirmed the working design presentation was already in the shared folder; it was the Project Manager's own presentation that was only in e-mail, and she said she would figure it out.

"age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting" overstates the transcript; the Marketing Expert suggested defining the group by money to spend and how recently they bought a TV, and the Project Manager suggested defining objectives instead of a target group. Nobody said lifestyle or attitude.
No owners are given for any next step, though the transcript assigns the age-breakdown e-mail to the Marketing Expert and the minutes/slides upload to the Project Manager.
strengths: Most complete coverage of the research: 100 subjects, 75%/80%, 60+ segment, 50%+ losing remotes, RSI, 10% of buttons, 65% zapping, and the LCD screen mention.
Captures both prices (25 euro retail, 12.50 euro production), scope limits, corporate identity details including the Rs, the sliding panel idea, and the cradle rationale.
Agreed functions list matches what the Project Manager summarised at the end, and post-meeting steps (questionnaire, summary, 30 minutes individual work, personal coach e-mails) are included.
Well organised and readable for someone who missed the meeting.
weaknesses: The shared-folder next step is attributed to the wrong presentation and describes a fix that was abandoned in the meeting.
Target group line reads as more settled than it was; the open question is only implied.
No owners on next steps and no timestamps.

evaluations.label: C
errors: "Speaker 5 discussed the technical interface, noting the need to balance conventional button placement with novel features like potential LCD screens or sliding hatches": the User Interface Designer's presentation mentioned neither; the LCD screen came from the Marketing Expert's research and the sliding panel came up in later discussion, first raised by the Marketing Expert.
"Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition": management ruled out teletext; voice recognition was dropped by the team in discussion on cost grounds.

"Action Items (none)" is wrong; the Project Manager assigned a questionnaire and summary to everyone, individual concept work by role, said she would post minutes and slides, and the Marketing Expert said she would e-mail more age data.
"Unresolved Questions: Would adding a find my remote beep function fit within budget?" was never asked; the group agreed the finder function fit the goal with no budget objection.
"Is it feasible to include advanced features without exceeding the production cost limit?" is an invented framing; the only cost debate was about voice recognition.
"charging cradle ... to improve convenience and location tracking" stretches the Industrial Designer's point that a cradle might keep the remote in one place.
strengths: Core numbers (75%, 80%, 10%, 12.50 euro, 25 euro, 100 subjects, 12:13 start, 40 minutes) are correct.
The outline section follows the meeting order and correctly records scope, corporate identity, the agreed functions, and the target group as discussed rather than decided.
Correctly notes the team weighed 15-35 against a broader range.
weaknesses: Speakers are labelled Speaker 2, 3, 4, 5 with no mapping to roles, so a reader cannot tell who said what.
Summary section conflates presentations and invents open questions that were not raised.
Declares no action items when several were assigned; omits the shared-folder issue and the Marketing Expert's promised data.
Duplication between Summary and Outline adds length without adding information.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Action item owners are given as "Speaker 1" while the body calls the same person "the project lead"; the label is unexplained and inconsistent with the rest of the notes.

The action items list omits the Marketing Expert's commitment to e-mail further age-breakdown numbers before the next meeting, and omits the questionnaire/summary and individual concept work as owned actions (they appear only in the body).
strengths: Every factual claim checked against the transcript holds: research numbers, four components, infrared choice, teletext and TV-only scope, 25 euro retail, 12.50 euro production limit, slogan, sliding panel, chip transmission caution, cradle and living-room space.
Correctly states that the target demographic was left open and lists the ranges that were floated (15-35, under 65, 20-55) plus the idea of defining by spending ability.
Correctly records the shared-folder situation: working design presentation uploaded, Project Manager's presentation not on the server and she will sort it out.
Section lead-ins plus timestamps make it easy to navigate and verify.
weaknesses: Action item list is thin (two items, both for the project lead) and misses the Marketing Expert's data e-mail.
Omits a few research details others caught: 65% zapping, the 60+ segment, the LCD screen mention, and the Real Reaction source.
Some bullets are generic ("Each area had a corresponding concept or work focus") where the transcript gives specifics.

rationale: D is the only set with no substantive factual errors; it correctly leaves the target group open, gets the shared-folder situation right, and covers decisions, scope, prices and next steps, losing points only for a thin action list and a stray Speaker 1 label. B is the most complete on research and requirements but misattributes which presentation was missing from the shared folder and gives no owners. A is mostly accurate but terse, wrongly records 15-35 as the decided target group, and its action items are loosely supported while the real assignments are missing. C ranks last: it conflates presentations, misattributes the voice recognition decision to management, invents unresolved questions, declares no action items when several were assigned, and uses unmapped speaker numbers.
